MEA-2.6.failed_clause: Level 2 needs every system in the dated scope register evaluated, and each residual risk accepted with the accepting role and the date. No scope register is in the pack, so coverage cannot be counted, and EV-481 names the acceptor (Model Owner) but gives no acceptance date.

MEA-2.7.boundary_note: The artefact is withheld, not shown to be absent. Absence cannot be established, so the score is NA rather than 0.
MEA-2.7.failed_clause: The red-team report (CRHP-RT-2026-06) is held under legal privilege and its contents are not available (EV-491). Adversarial testing, resilience documentation and per-system coverage cannot be assessed.

MEA-2.8.boundary_note: EV-500 is a dated risk assessment, and EV-501 shows the notice and letters exist. EV-502 limits the assessment to CTA only. The adequacy-test artefact is missing, so the score is level 1.
MEA-2.8.failed_clause: Level 2 needs a separate dated adequacy test of the documentation carried out with the affected population, with findings recorded. No such test is in the pack.

MEA-2.9.boundary_note: Level 2 rests on EV-510 (explanation method and guidance) and EV-511 (validation). EV-512 shows the guidance is stale since the 2026-07 refresh and EV-511 is undated. The anchor for level 2 does not require currency, so the score is 2, but this is a borderline call.
MEA-2.9.failed_clause: Level 3 needs measured user comprehension and explanation-use rates per release. EV-511 is a one-off 20-case study with no per-release measurement or usage rate.

MEA-3.1.boundary_note: Level 1 is met by EV-560 (named owner, monthly cadence, log). Any gap in minutes or closure records keeps the score at level 1.
MEA-3.1.failed_clause: Level 2 needs dated minutes for every review month in the period. Only 8 of 9 months have minutes, and the skipped month has no note. Emergent-risk closure records also cover only 7 of 23 entries.

MEA-3.2.boundary_note: Level 2 is met by EV-570 (three methods with stated limits) and EV-571 (two methods used, with records). EV-572 shows narrow application, which is not a level 2 clause.
MEA-3.2.failed_clause: Level 3 needs method-comparison results and stated confidence per hard-to-assess case. Each method was used once on a different risk, so there is no comparison, and no confidence statements are named.

MEA-3.3.boundary_note: EV-580 (volume of 214) and EV-581 (appeal process with recorded outcomes) satisfy two of the three level 2 artefacts. The missing third artefact gives level 1.
MEA-3.3.failed_clause: Level 2 needs a dated record showing that feedback analysis produced a named change or decision. EV-582 says the analysis is not linked to system changes in any recorded way.

MEA-4.1.boundary_note: Level 2 is met by EV-590 (tests on production replay data) and EV-591 (clinical and adjuster input recorded).
MEA-4.1.failed_clause: Level 3 needs the lab-versus-production performance gap measured and reported. No gap measurement is named, and the vendor benchmarks in EV-592 were not validated against CRHP data.

MEA-4.2.boundary_note: Level 2 is met by EV-600 (expert reviews) and EV-601 (independence recorded for Internal Audit). The Clinical Advisory Panel member who advises the CTA product team is a recorded conflict, which makes this a borderline call; the anchor only requires that independence be recorded.
MEA-4.2.failed_clause: Level 3 needs review coverage and the resolution outcome of disagreements measured. EV-602 gives only a qualitative count (two comments led to re-analysis), with no coverage measure or resolution metric.

MEA-4.3.boundary_note: Level 1 is met by EV-610 (drift monitoring detecting changes). EV-612 gives latency and action-time medians, but there is no target and no named reviewing body, so level 3 would also fail.
MEA-4.3.failed_clause: Level 2 needs every detected change to have a dated root-cause analysis and a recorded corrective action, tied together in a change log. No change log is named, and only the 2026-08 decline has a documented fix. The 2026-04 corrective action is not evidenced. EV-613 also says 6 systems had change events, against only 2 declines analysed.
